mainTopic: Vows with a harmless second meaning, how a careless vower is treated, and teachings on habits, modesty and בושה that lead toward or away from sin.
overview: The משנה lists four cases where a person makes what sounds like a real נדר and then says he meant a harmless second meaning of his words. רבי מאיר says such a person needs no התרה, but if he asks for one, we punish him and are strict with him. The חכמים say we release him through some other פתח and teach him not to take vows lightly. The גמרא asks how רבי מאיר can say both things. רב יהודה answers that a תלמיד חכם needs no התרה, while an עם הארץ who asks is treated strictly. A ברייתא about a נזיר who broke his נזירות shows what the 'punishment' is: he must keep the vow for a while before a חכם will release it. רב יוסף and רב אחא בר יעקב then judge a בית דין that releases him too early. Next, a ברייתא warns against habits that lead to sin, and the גמרא brings teachings on modesty, on how בושה leads to יראת חטא, and four things the מלאכי השרת told רבי יוחנן בן דהבאי. The amud ends as the גמרא starts a contradiction from a question put to אימא שלום, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Cases of חרם and קרבן with a harmless second meaning
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens with two cases where someone vows with the words חרם or קרבן and later claims he meant a fishing net or a gift to a king.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone vowed using the word 'חרם' and then said, 'I only meant a fishing net.' Someone vowed using the word 'קרבן' and then said, 'I only meant gifts given to kings.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists its first two cases. In each one, a vow word has a second, everyday meaning that the person says he meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חרם normally means something set aside for the בית המקדש, but it also means a fishing net. קרבן normally means an offering to ה׳, but it can also mean a gift brought to a king. If he really meant the everyday meaning, his words never made anything forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (the text being studied)
Something set aside for the בית המקדש; a vow word
A fishing net (literally, 'the net of the sea')
An offering; a common vow word
Gifts brought to kings

steps.confusionAlert: The person is not saying he made a vow and regrets it. He is saying his words never meant a vow in the first place.

phrases.english: MISHNA
One vowed with the word 'cherem,'
phrases.notes: He said something like 'this is חרם to me,' meaning forbidden like something given to the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: and then said: I only vowed
with the 'cherem' of the sea, a fishing net.
Or one vowed with 'korban,' and then said:
I only vowed
with the 'offerings' of kings, gifts to a king.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָדַר בְּחֵרֶם, וְאָמַר: לֹא נָדַרְתִּי אֶלָּא בְּחֶרְמוֹ שֶׁל יָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opening of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up cases where a vow word is reinterpreted by the speaker as a non-vow meaning.

steps.title: Cases of 'my self' as a bone and 'my wife' as a divorced wife
steps.stepSummary: Two more cases: 'עצמי' explained as a bone he set aside, and 'אשתי' explained as his first wife whom he already divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone said, 'I myself am a קרבן,' and then said, 'I meant a bone I set aside to vow by.' Someone said, 'My wife may not benefit from me (קונם),' and then said, 'I meant my first wife, whom I divorced.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds two more cases of the same kind, where the person gives his words a second meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word עצמי can mean 'myself' or 'my bone,' so he claims he only meant a bone he had put aside. 'My wife' could refer to a former wife, and a vow about her does nothing to his current marriage. In both cases, his explanation would cancel the vow.

keyTerms.meaning: Myself, or my bone (the word has both meanings)
A bone
A vow word meaning 'forbidden like a קרבן'
Whom I divorced

phrases.english: 'I myself am hereby an offering,' and then said:
I only vowed with a bone
phrases.notes: עצמי can mean 'myself' or 'my bone.' He claims he meant the bone.

phrases.english: that I set aside for myself to vow with;
'Konam, my wife may not benefit from me,' and then said:
I only vowed about my first wife
whom I divorced —

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי עַצְמִי קׇרְבָּן, וְאָמַר: לֹא נָדַרְתִּי אֶלָּא בְּעֶצֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of cases begun in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two more cases of the same pattern: the speaker gives his vow words a harmless meaning.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: no need to ask, and if they ask, be strict
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר rules that these people don't need התרה, but if they ask for it, we punish them and are strict with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: For all these cases, they do not need to ask a חכם to release them. If they do ask, we punish them and are strict with them. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the ruling for all four cases, according to רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If his explanation is true, there was never a vow, so there is nothing to release. If he comes asking anyway, it shows he is not really sure of his own excuse. So רבי מאיר holds we are strict with him and do not release the vow.

keyTerms.meaning: Asking a חכם to release a vow (התרת נדרים)
We punish
We are strict
These are the words of רבי מאיר

steps.confusionAlert: 'אין נשאלין' here does not mean they are forbidden to ask. It means they don't need to ask, because by their own explanation no vow took effect.

phrases.english: For all of them, they do not need to request release.
But if they did request release —
we punish them and are strict with them.
These are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל כּוּלָּן אֵין נִשְׁאָלִין לָהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling for the cases listed in steps 1 and 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No התרה is needed. If they ask anyway, the court is strict and punishes them (רבי מאיר).

steps.title: חכמים: release them another way and teach them
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים disagree. We release the vow using a different opening, and we teach the person not to take vows lightly.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: we open a way to release the vow from some other angle, and we teach them, so that they will not treat vows lightly.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים argue with רבי מאיר about the person who comes asking. They release him, but not through his word games.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of punishing, the חכם finds a פתח, a reason for regret, that has nothing to do with the double meaning of his words. They also teach him a lesson, so people won't play games with vow language. Both sides agree that such vows are a problem; they disagree only on how to handle them.

keyTerms.meaning: The majority of the Sages
We open a way out for them, a reason to release the vow
From another angle, not from his wording
Lightheadedness, not taking something seriously

steps.whatToRemember: Four cases where the vow words have a harmless second meaning. רבי מאיר: no התרה is needed, but if they ask, we are strict. חכמים: we release them through some other פתח and teach them not to treat נדרים lightly.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how seriously חז״ל treat vow language: even playful double meanings are discouraged, whether by being strict or by teaching the person a lesson.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
We open an opening for them from another place,
phrases.notes: He means the חכם finds a reason to release the vow that has nothing to do with the double meaning of the words.

phrases.english: and we teach them —

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִנְהֲגוּ קַלּוּת רֹאשׁ בִּנְדָרִים.
phrases.english: so that they will not act lightly with vows.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: פּוֹתְחִין לָהֶן פֶּתַח מִמָּקוֹם אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי מאיר's strict treatment in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The vow is released through an unrelated פתח, and the person is taught not to take vows lightly.

steps.title: The משנה seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רבי מאיר says these vows need no התרה, yet also speaks of punishing people who ask for one.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: This itself is difficult. You said they do not need to ask about these vows, and then it teaches that if they ask, we punish them and are strict with them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by finding a problem inside the משנה's own words. רבי מאיר's two statements seem to clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the vow needs no התרה, it is not a real vow. So why would we punish someone for asking, as if the vow were real? The two halves of the ruling seem to point in opposite directions.

keyTerms.meaning: This itself is difficult. The text contradicts itself.
And then it teaches. It points to a later clause in the same text.

phrases.english: GEMARA: This itself is difficult:
you said: they do not need to ask about them,
phrases.notes: This is רבי מאיר's ruling from step 3. 'Ask' means asking a חכם to release the vow.

phrases.english: and then it teaches:
if they asked, we punish them
and are strict with them?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא גּוּפָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the גמרא and challenges רבי מאיר's ruling from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's ruling in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No need for התרה means the vow is not binding, yet punishing those who ask treats it as binding.

steps.title: רב יהודה: the ruling depends on who the person is
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה reads the משנה as two cases: a תלמיד חכם needs no התרה, while an עם הארץ who asks is punished and treated strictly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said, this is what it teaches: none of them need to ask. When is that said? For a תלמיד חכם. But an עם הארץ who comes to ask is punished and treated strictly.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה solves the contradiction by saying the two halves of the ruling are about two different kinds of people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תלמיד חכם knows these words never made a real vow, so he needs nothing. An עם הארץ who comes to ask shows he thinks his vow is real. So we treat him strictly, to teach him not to play with vows.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches. The משנה is read in a new way.
When is this said? It limits a rule.
A Torah scholar
An unlearned person

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up רב יהודה here, who is an אמורא, with רבי יהודה in the ברייתא below, who is a תנא. They are different people.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said, this is what it teaches:
and all of them do not need asking,
when is this said? With a Torah scholar,
but with an unlearned person who comes to ask,
we punish him and are strict with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, הָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: different people get different rulings
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both halves of the ruling seemed to be about the same person.
steps.terutzMaskana: No התרה is needed for a תלמיד חכם. An עם הארץ who asks is punished and treated strictly.

steps.title: What does 'punishing' him mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא understands what 'strict' means but asks what the 'punishment' actually is.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that we are strict: we don't open the vow for him with regret. But what does 'we punish him' look like?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts רב יהודה's answer and now asks to define one of its words. This sets up the ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being 'strict' is clear: the חכם will not release the vow just because the man regrets it, and must find some other opening. But 'punish' must mean something more, and the גמרא wants to know what.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense. The גמרא agrees with one part before asking about another.
Regret. The usual opening for releasing a vow.
What does it look like? What is the case?

phrases.english: It makes sense that we are strict:
that we do not open for him with regret,
phrases.notes: Usually a חכם releases a vow by finding that the person regrets it. Here that easy route is closed.

phrases.english: but 'we punish', what does it look like?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא מַחְמִירִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to define the word 'punish' from רב יהודה's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical form the 'punishment' of the עם הארץ takes

steps.title: The ברייתא: keep the rules before being released
steps.stepSummary: A נזיר who broke his נזירות is not helped until he keeps its rules for as many days as he broke them. This shows what 'punishing' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: someone who became a נזיר and broke his נזירות is not helped until he keeps the rules for as many days as he broke them. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. The 'punishment' is that the person must first keep his vow for some time before a חכם will release it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before releasing the vow, the חכם makes the person live with it as if it were binding. This matches the days he ignored it. In the same way, the עם הארץ in our משנה must keep his vow for a while before we release him.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught. It introduces a ברייתא.
The vow and status of a נזיר
We help or deal with him, here by releasing the vow

phrases.aramaic: כִּדְתַנְיָא: מִי שֶׁנָּזַר וְעָבַר עַל נְזִירוּתוֹ —
phrases.english: As it was taught: one who vowed to be a nazir and broke his naziriteship,
we do not deal with him
until he keeps it as forbidden
for as many days as he treated it as permitted.
These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The punishment is that he must first keep the vow for a period before it is released.

steps.title: רבי יוסי limits the rule for a long נזירות
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says the 'equal days' rule is only for a short נזירות. For a long one, thirty days is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: when is this said? For a short נזירות. But for a long נזירות, thirty days is enough for him.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the same ברייתא, רבי יוסי adds a limit to רבי יהודה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a short נזירות, he must make up all the days he broke. For a long נזירות, that could be far too heavy, so thirty days of keeping it is enough before the חכם releases him. Either way the main idea stays: he must first keep the vow for a while.

keyTerms.meaning: A short נזירות, the basic thirty days
A long נזירות, more than thirty days
It is enough for him

steps.whatToRemember: These vows need no התרה for a תלמיד חכם. But an עם הארץ who asks is treated strictly, so regret alone won't release him. He is also 'punished': he must keep the vow for a time before release, like the נזיר in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
When is this said? With a short naziriteship.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בִּנְזִירוּת מְרוּבָּה — דַּיּוֹ שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם.
phrases.english: But with a long naziriteship, thirty days is enough for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא, adding רבי יוסי's limit to רבי יהודה's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'equal days' rule is for a short נזירות. For a long נזירות, thirty days is enough.

steps.title: A court that helps him too early is acting wrongly
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says that since the רבנן said we do not help this person, a בית דין that does help him is not acting properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Since the רבנן said we do not deal with him, a בית דין that does deal with him is not acting properly.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף adds a practical point to the 'punishment' we just learned. He judges any בית דין that ignores the rule and helps this person right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 8-9 taught that this person must wait before anyone helps undo his vow. רב יוסף now says that a בית דין that undoes the vow early has done something wrong. He calls it improper, but he does not name a penalty.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not deal with him or help him (here, we do not undo his vow right away)
A Jewish court (בית דין)
Is not acting properly

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן אֵין נִזְקָקִים לוֹ,
phrases.english: Since the Sages say we do not deal with him,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the careless vower from the last few steps, the one we make wait before undoing his vow.

phrases.english: a court that does deal with him
is not acting properly.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: הוֹאִיל וְאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן אֵין נִזְקָקִים לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from how the vower is punished to how a בית דין that ignores that rule is judged.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בית דין that undoes the vow before the waiting period is over is not acting properly.

steps.title: A stricter view: the court is put in נידוי
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב says something stronger: whoever undoes this vow too early is put in נידוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב says: We put him in נידוי.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a harsher reaction to the same case. He does more than call the act improper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף only said the בית דין acted wrongly. רב אחא בר יעקב gives a real penalty: נידוי for whoever undoes the vow too early. This shows how seriously the rule is taken.

keyTerms.meaning: We put him in נידוי (excommunicate him)

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov says:
We excommunicate him.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the one who undid the vow too early, not the person who made the vow.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: מְשַׁמְּתִינַן לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a stricter view than רב יוסף on the same case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever undoes the vow too early is put in נידוי.
steps.whatToRemember: Under רבי מאיר's approach, a careless vower is not helped right away. A בית דין that helps him early acts improperly (רב יוסף) and is even put in נידוי (רב אחא בר יעקב).

steps.title: Don't get used to making vows
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the חכמים of the משנה and brings a ברייתא: don't make vows a habit, because in the end you will treat even שבועות lightly.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the חכמים say: We open a פתח for him, etc.' A ברייתא teaches: Never get used to making נדרים, because in the end you will betray שבועות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section by quoting the opinion of the חכמים in the משנה. Then it brings a ברייתא with a lesson about not getting used to vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים help the person find an opening (פתח) to undo his vow, and they teach him not to vow so easily. The ברייתא gives the reason: a person who vows all the time stops taking his word seriously, and in the end he will break even a שבועה, which is more serious than a נדר.

keyTerms.meaning: We give him an 'opening', a reason that lets his vow be undone
Used to it; doing it out of habit
To betray or misuse oaths

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים פּוֹתְחִין לוֹ פֶּתַח כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: And the Sages say: We open an opening for him, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה again. 'Etc.' means the rest of the line there, which is about teaching him not to vow so easily.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא: לְעוֹלָם אַל תְּהִי רָגִיל בַּנְּדָרִים,
phrases.english: It was taught: Never be accustomed to vows,
because in the end you will betray oaths.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים פּוֹתְחִין לוֹ פֶּתַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רבי מאיר's view and turns to the חכמים's view in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Making vows a habit leads in the end to breaking even שבועות.

steps.title: More bad habits that lead to sin
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא goes on: don't be too close with an עם הארץ (he will feed you טבל), with an עם הארץ כהן (he will feed you תרומה), and don't talk too much with a woman (it leads to ניאוף).
steps.simpleTranslation: And don't be often with an עם הארץ, because in the end he will feed you טבל. Don't be often with a כהן who is an עם הארץ, because in the end he will feed you תרומה. And don't talk too much with a woman, because in the end you will come to adultery.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא lists more habits that seem small but slowly lead to real sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every line has the same form: a habit, and then 'in the end' the sin it leads to. An עם הארץ is not careful about מעשרות, so his food may be טבל. A friendly כהן עם הארץ may share his תרומה with you, and a non-כהן may not eat it.

keyTerms.meaning: An unlearned person who is not careful with מצוות like מעשרות
Produce that has not had תרומה and מעשרות taken off; forbidden to eat
A gift to the כהן; a non-כהן may not eat it
Adultery

phrases.aramaic: וְאַל תְּהִי רָגִיל אֵצֶל עַם הָאָרֶץ,
phrases.english: And do not be regularly around an ignoramus,
because in the end he will feed you untithed produce.

phrases.aramaic: אַל תְּהִי רָגִיל אֵצֶל כֹּהֵן עַם הָאָרֶץ,
phrases.english: Do not be regularly around an ignorant priest,
because in the end he will feed you terumah.
And do not talk too much with a woman,
because in the end you will come to adultery.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַל תְּהִי רָגִיל אֵצֶל עַם הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with more warnings in the same form.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Habits that seem harmless (being close with an עם הארץ, talking too much with women) slowly lead to real sins.

steps.title: Staring at women leads to sin
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא ברבי יאשיה says that whoever stares at women will come to sin, and whoever looks at a woman's 'heel' will have children who are not proper.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אחא ברבי יאשיה says: Whoever gazes at women will in the end come to sin. And whoever looks at a woman's heel will have children who are not proper.
steps.whatsHappening: A תנא continues the theme of the last line and warns against looking at women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא spoke about talking with women. רבי אחא ברבי יאשיה adds looking. He gives two results: staring leads to sin, and looking at the 'heel' brings a punishment through one's children.

keyTerms.meaning: One who gazes or watches
Her heel (explained in step 16)
Proper, decent

phrases.english: Rabbi Acha son of Rabbi Yoshiya says:
Anyone who gazes at women
will in the end come to sin.
And anyone who looks at the heel of a woman
will have children who are not proper.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַחָא בְּרַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הַצּוֹפֶה בְּנָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from talking with women to looking at women.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Staring at women leads to sin, and looking at a woman's 'heel' is punished through one's children.

steps.title: This includes even his own wife when she is a נדה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the warning about the 'heel' applies even to a man's own wife while she is a נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: And even with his wife when she is a נדה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף makes the last statement wider. It does not apply only to other women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think a man's own wife is never included in this warning. רב יוסף says that when she is a נדה and forbidden to him, the same warning applies to her too.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman in her time of impurity, when she is forbidden to her husband

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: And even with his wife when she is a niddah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: וּבְאִשְׁתּוֹ נִדָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Makes the case in step 14 wider to include his own wife when she is a נדה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The warning includes a man's own wife while she is a נדה.

steps.title: What 'heel' really means
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains that 'heel' is a polite way of saying the private place, which is in line with the heel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: The 'heel' that was taught means the place of uncleanliness, which lines up opposite the heel.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש explains one word from step 14. He tells us what 'heel' really refers to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It would be strange for looking at an actual heel to bring such a punishment. ריש לקיש explains that the word is a polite way to say the private place, and it is called 'heel' because it is in line with the heel.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'place of uncleanliness', a polite way of saying the private place
That was taught (in the teaching we just learned)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'heel' simply as the foot. ריש לקיש says it is a polite way of saying something else.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
The 'heel' that was taught
means the place of uncleanliness,
which lines up opposite the heel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: עֲקֵבָהּ דְּקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains a word in רבי אחא ברבי יאשיה's statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Heel' here is a polite way of saying the private place.

steps.title: בושה leads to fear of sin
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads a פסוק to teach that בושה brings a person to יראת חטא. So being a person who feels shame is a good sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: 'That His fear may be upon your faces': this is shame. 'So that you will not sin': this teaches that shame leads to fear of sin. From here they said: It is a good sign in a person that he feels shame easily.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that learns from a פסוק how much בושה is worth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Fear on your faces' is read as shame, because shame shows on the face. The next words, 'so that you will not sin', show that shame is what keeps a person from sinning. So a person who feels shame easily has a good sign.

keyTerms.meaning: Shame, a sense of embarrassment
Fear of sin
A person who feels shame easily
From here they said

phrases.english: It was taught: 'That His fear may be upon your faces'
this is shame.
'So that you will not sin'

phrases.aramaic: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהַבּוּשָׁה מְבִיאָה לִידֵי יִרְאַת חֵטְא.
phrases.english: teaches that shame leads to fear of sin.
From here they said:
It is a good sign in a person that he feels shame easily.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: ״בַּעֲבוּר תִּהְיֶה יִרְאָתוֹ עַל פְּנֵיכֶם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching about בושה, still on the theme of what keeps a person from sin.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בושה leads to יראת חטא, so feeling shame is a good sign in a person.

steps.title: Without בושה, a sign his ancestors were not at סיני
steps.stepSummary: אחרים say a person who feels shame will not sin quickly. A person with no בושת פנים shows that his ancestors did not stand at הר סיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: אחרים say: Any person who feels shame will not sin quickly. And one who has no shame on his face, it is known that his ancestors did not stand at הר סיני.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion, called אחרים, ends the teaching about בושה with a positive side and a negative side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The positive side: shame slows a person down before he sins. The negative side: having no shame at all shows that his family did not stand at הר סיני, where the פסוק from step 17 was said.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Others say', an opinion given without naming the person
Shame that shows on the face
Mount Sinai, where the Torah was given

steps.whatToRemember: בושה is a protection against sin. It goes back to the giving of the Torah at הר סיני, and a person with no shame at all shows his ancestors were not there.

phrases.english: Others say:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אָדָם הַמִּתְבַּיֵּישׁ, לֹא בִּמְהֵרָה הוּא חוֹטֵא.
phrases.english: Any person who feels shame will not quickly sin.
And one who has no shame on his face,

phrases.aramaic: בְּיָדוּעַ שֶׁלֹּא עָמְדוּ אֲבוֹתָיו עַל הַר סִינַי.
phrases.english: it is known that his ancestors did not stand at Mount Sinai.
phrases.notes: The פסוק from step 17 was said at הר סיני, so the shame it talks about goes back to that moment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲחֵרִים אוֹמְרִים: כׇּל אָדָם הַמִּתְבַּיֵּישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, stronger way of saying the lesson of step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Feeling shame keeps a person from sinning quickly; having no shame shows his ancestors did not stand at הר סיני.

steps.title: Four things the angels told רבי יוחנן בן דהבאי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן דהבאי says the מלאכי השרת told him four reasons why children are born lame, mute, deaf, or blind. Each one is tied to an immodest behavior during marital relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן דהבאי said: The מלאכי השרת told me four things. Why are some people born lame? Because their parents 'overturn their table' (they are together in an unusual way). Why are some born mute? Because they kiss that private place. Why are some born deaf? Because they talk during relations. Why are some born blind? Because they stare at that private place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching that lists four immodest behaviors and the harm each one can bring to the children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the theme from step 14, where looking at the 'heel' leads to children who are not proper. Here the idea gets more detailed: each specific behavior is matched to a specific defect. The last item, staring at 'that place,' fits closely with the earlier steps about looking.

keyTerms.meaning: The ministering angels
Lame people
Mute people (cannot speak)
Deaf people
Blind people
Marital relations (a polite word)

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching is the base that the גמרא is about to challenge with the story of אימא שלום, so you need to have these four items clear.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Dehavai said:

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים סָחוּ לִי מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת:
phrases.english: Four things the ministering angels told me:
Lame people, for what reason do they come about?
Because they overturn their table.
phrases.notes: 'Overturning the table' is a polite way of saying the couple is together in an unusual way.

phrases.english: Mute people, for what reason do they come about?
Because they kiss that place.
phrases.notes: 'That place' means the private place, the same idea as the 'heel' back in step 16.

phrases.english: Deaf people, for what reason do they come about?
Because they talk during relations.
Blind people, for what reason do they come about?
Because they stare at that place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן דַּהֲבַאי, אַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים סָחוּ לִי מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of modesty and its effect on children, giving four specific behaviors and their results.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four immodest behaviors during marital relations (unusual manner, kissing that place, talking, staring at that place) lead to children who are lame, mute, deaf, or blind.

steps.title: Setting up a contradiction from אימא שלום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to raise a contradiction to רבי יוחנן בן דהבאי from a story where people asked אימא שלום a 'why' question. Only the opening words appear here.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the גמרא raises a contradiction: They asked אימא שלום: For what reason...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. It starts quoting a story about אימא שלום that seems to clash with what רבי יוחנן בן דהבאי just said, and the story continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ורמינהו tells us a contradiction is coming: another source seems to say the opposite of step 19. We don't yet know what the question to אימא שלום is or how it clashes; that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And they threw them together' — the גמרא points out a contradiction between two sources
The wife of רבי אליעזר. People put a question to her, and her answer (on the next amud) is the source being quoted.
For what reason

steps.confusionAlert: This step is not finished. Don't try to figure out the contradiction yet; the rest of the question to אימא שלום comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
They asked Imma Shalom:
For what reason
phrases.notes: The question breaks off here and continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a contradiction against the teaching of רבי יוחנן בן דהבאי in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The four teachings of רבי יוחנן בן דהבאי in step 19.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A story about אימא שלום will be brought that seems to conflict with step 19; the details continue on the next amud.
